rows.title: Member
rows.body: Member — baseline rates, milestone rewards path, points never expire.

rows.title: Gold
rows.body: Gold — 5 nights or 10,000 EQCs; bonus points on stays and enhanced recognition.

rows.title: Platinum
rows.body: Platinum — 15 nights or 30,000 EQCs; stronger earn bonus and elite benefits where available.

rows.title: Diamond
rows.body: Diamond — 35 nights or 70,000 EQCs; top mainstream tier with upgrades and milestone rewards where published.

rows.title: Titanium
rows.body: Titanium — 55 nights or 110,000 EQCs; highest published tier including Titanium Travel Award where offered.
Model net after distribution, member discounts, and redemption—strongest when direct/member mix supports upper-midscale (Radisson family) ADR.
Elite recognition and breakfast/F&B promises become labor and COGS—staff to brand standards before campaigns.
CRS/PMS loyalty integration and campaign tooling are mandatory—budget cutover and training.

Park Inn by Radisson (Choice) fits when you want upper-midscale (Radisson family) Choice distribution with clear prototype economics and Choice Privileges participation—not a mismatched tier (e.g., Country Inn & Suites by Radisson (Choice) vs Park Inn by Radisson (Choice) without comparing fee stack and amenity requirements). Best with operator tier experience, honest ramp plan, and FDD-backed channel mix. Weaker where market ADR cannot support required product or PIP exceeds conversion ROI.
